background_story: Azalea was a bright and vibrant young woman who lived in a small village in Iran. She loved nothing more than celebrating the ancient Persian New Year, Noruz, with her family and friends. Every year, Azalea would help her mother prepare the traditional haft-seen table, carefully arranging the symbolic items such as sabzeh, senjed, and samanu. She took great pride in her cultural heritage and spent hours cooking traditional Noruz dishes like sabzi polo and kuku sabzi. As the clock struck midnight on the spring equinox, Azalea would join her loved ones in jumping over fires, symbolizing the purification of the soul. She believed that the spirit of renewal and rejuvenation that came with Noruz was a powerful reminder of the beauty and resilience of life. Azalea's love for Noruz was contagious, and her enthusiasm brought joy to all those around her.
